title: Wholesome Algerian Fenugreek Tagine
description: A briny, juicy, monsoon-inspired Algerian dish featuring fenugreek and a diabetic-friendly miso-marinate.
instructions: In a blender or food processor, puree the miso paste with 2 tablespoons of water until smooth.
In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and lemon zest.
Add the fenugreek leaves, capers, green olives, preserved lemon, and chopped cilantro to the bowl and mix well.
Add the chili peppers, onion, garlic, and lemongrass to the bowl and mix well.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion mixture to the saucepan and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and lightly browned.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, miso paste mixture, and fenugreek-infused water to the saucepan and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the flavors have melded together and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the fenugreek leaves and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley and a sprinkle of lemon zest.
Cover and refrigerate any leftovers for up to 3 days.
Reheat the leftovers over low heat, stirring occasionally, until warmed through.
